title: The way back down
hookLine: the morning after a big day, and a map that sends the traveler back down
carry: in tantra, the everyday world is shakti too
tomorrow: summer is a blank calendar. where does a year of service start?

lines: THE MORNING AFTER THE BIG DAY.
SHE MEETS SHIVA AT THE CROWN.
cards: The day after a big thing is strange. The wedding's over, the game is won, the show has closed, and the next morning there's still a sink full of dishes and a quiz on Tuesday.
The old chakra map has a page for that morning. In the Sat-Cakra-Nirupana, kundalini reaches the crown and meets Shiva. Then the text does something easy to miss.
She's led back down, by the same road, to where she started.

teach.b: The summit is the meeting the whole rising was for. But the text doesn't leave the meditator floating up there. She returns, lotus by lotus, to the base.
The map has a way home drawn on it. Many teachers read that return through one of tantra's central teachings: the world isn't a trap to escape.
It's Shakti, the Goddess as power, moving. So she doesn't abandon the body and the day; she comes back into them. That's the line to take to dinner: in tantra, the everyday world is Shakti too.
The science seat closes this run its own way. What is this picture for?

teach.h: NOT A SCAN, NOT A DIAGNOSIS.
teach.b: It isn't a scan. It isn't a diagnosis either, so nobody should use it to decide what's wrong with their body; that's a doctor's work. Two maps can disagree and both be useful.
And a good map gets you back.
Now step back, because this is the last day of the part, and the whole of it comes into view. Tantra turned out to be a family of texts and practices, not a rumor.
The Vijnana Bhairava gave short ways to turn attention inward.

teach.h: THE MAP ENDS AT THE BOTTOM.
teach.b: The Sri Yantra drew the Goddess in lines and circles. The chakras drew the body as a road for the mind. Each one, framed fairly, asks to be practiced and understood before it's judged.
And each one, like this map, sends a person back to an ordinary life: the dishes, the quiz, the people at the table.

how: In kundalini practice as the tantric texts describe it, the meditator brings the rising power back down to the base before ending; traditional teachers stress returning to ordinary life after practice.

games.q: what does “the chakras as a map” mean?
o: a road up to a meeting, then back home
a ladder you climb once and never come down
a checklist of organs to fix one by one

games.q: the last page, and the part — tap the pairs.
p: lotus by lotus, back to the base
short ways to turn attention inward

s: in tantra, the everyday world is something to escape
many tantric teachers read the world as Shakti, the Goddess as power; the map comes home to it.
a chakra chart can tell you what's wrong with your body
it's a map for meditation, not a diagnosis; health questions belong with a doctor.
in the text, kundalini meets Shiva at the crown
that meeting is what the rising was for, and then she comes home.

games.q: your uncle reads a chakra chart, decides his chest pain is 'a blocked heart chakra', and skips the doctor. what does the science seat say?
o: the map isn't a diagnosis; chest pain is a question for a doctor, today.
follow the chart; an old map knows the body better than tests.
ignore both the chart and the doctor, and wait to see.
games.why: the chakras are a map for meditation, not a scan or a diagnosis. a doctor reads the body; the map was never drawn for that job.

practice: Stand, if you can, and walk slowly for a minute, across the room and back or in a small circle. Feel each step land, heel then toe, as if you were coming down a long road and arriving home.
Then sit, and let the rest of the time be ordinary.

wordCard.voice: The chakras as a map: up to the crown for a meeting, then back down the same road, home to the base.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the name for the family of texts and practices this part has framed.

carryVoice: Your line: in tantra, the everyday world is Shakti too. The map ends at the bottom. And that closes the Tantras, framed.

sources.ref: Sat-Cakra-Nirupana (the thousand-petaled lotus above the head; kundalini's union with Shiva there; her return by the same path to the base)
Shakta and Shaiva tantric teaching that the world is Shakti, the power of Shiva (a common reading of the return)
